contract: cancel_cover_search with the requestId of an active search aborts CoverSearchManager's AbortController and, only when cancelSearch found the requestId, SocketAuthority emits cover_search_cancelled with {requestId} to the cancelling socket alone. The cancelled search emits no cover_search_result, cover_search_complete or cover_search_provider_error, also when the provider's answer arrives afterwards, and its requestId becomes reusable for a new search. Cancelling an unknown, empty or completed requestId, or cancelling from an unauthenticated socket, emits nothing and aborts nothing.
exceptions: force is not applicable: cancelling has no force or override variant; it either finds an active requestId or does nothing.

Cancelling another user's requestId is not asserted: the web client only cancels its own currentSearchRequestId, and upstream scopes cancellation by requestId alone, so a cross-user assertion would pin an authorization gap no client relies on.

invariants.contract: cancel_cover_search for an active requestId emits exactly one cover_search_cancelled {requestId} to the cancelling socket and none to another connection of the same user, another user's socket or an unauthenticated socket. After the cancellation the slow provider's answer arrives but produces no cover_search_result, cover_search_complete or cover_search_provider_error for that search. A cancelled requestId can start and complete a new search against another provider, while the cancelled provider's late answer still produces no result. Cancelling a completed requestId, a second cancellation of the same requestId, an unknown or empty requestId, an absent requestId, and a cancellation from an unauthenticated socket each emit no cover_search_cancelled and no error, and an unauthenticated cancellation does not abort an authenticated socket's active search, which still delivers its result and complete. A cancellation leaves the provider rows unchanged.
